tess: Quick note from an intro workshop — streaming demo using `async with client` + `async for` can leave the socket open when a kernel interrupt happens. Also saw the final event printed twice in a couple of runs. :grimacing:

ben: ugh. minimal repro? SSE or chunked?

tess: SSE-style from `client.stream_chat`. super tiny:
```py
async with Client(token=...) as c:
    async for e in c.stream_chat(model="sage-7B", messages=[...]):
        print(e.text)
```
Interrupt after a few events and sometimes last event duplicates; `ss` shows ESTABLISHED until kernel dies.

max: version matrix? any custom context managers?

tess: redwood-py 0.9.4, aiohttp 3.9.5, python 3.11. No custom middleware. Repro'd in colab.

ben: quick workaround: explicitly get iterator and close in finally:
```py
it = c.stream_chat().__aiter__()
try:
    async for x in it: ...
finally:
    await it.aclose()
```
That reliably closes socket. But mypy complains when you assign `it` because its type becomes `AsyncIterator[Any]`.

max: actionable items I see: 1) Make `aclose()` idempotent (no-op on second call) and guard final emit so duplicates don't happen. 2) Tighten typing: export `StreamIterator[T]` and make `stream_*()` return a generic iterator in our .pyi so users can annotate without cast gymnastics. 3) Short quickstart note about interrupts in notebooks.

tess: +1. Also propose a new ergonomic API `open_stream()` that returns a StreamHandle whose context manager returns the handle (not an independent generator) so context exit doesn't try to double-close. Example:
```py
async with c.open_stream('chat', model=...) as s:  # s: StreamHandle[ChatEvent]
    async for ev in s:
        ...
# s.close() can be awaited explicitly if deterministic shutdown needed
```

ben: runtime preference: keep deterministic `await it.aclose()` semantics. Implement idempotent `_aclose()` and make finalizer safe (suppress exceptions) rather than scheduling background closes. That keeps behavior predictable for users.

max: test plan: add pytest-asyncio test that starts a fake SSE server, consumes a few events, cancels the consumer task (simulate kernel interrupt) and assert: socket closed, final event emitted at most once, and no "Task exception was never retrieved" logs. Also add a mypy/stub test for the new StreamIterator alias.

tess: I'll attach the minimal colab and tiny aiohttp server repro to the issue and add the quickstart notebook note.

ci-bot: Created issue #4899 in redwood-python: "py-sdk streaming: duplicate final event & socket leak on interrupt; iterator typing ergonomics + open_stream proposal" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/issues/4899) :white_check_mark:

ben: thanks for the clear repro — saved us an awkward onboarding demo. I'll take the .pyi typing patch, max can own the runtime guard and tests.

max: will also add a short migration note in changelog so users know why `open_stream` exists and how it differs.

tess: thanks team :rocket:
